character.description: Leon Richter, 34, is a backend engineer at a logistics software company, where he has been passed over for team lead twice. Neat side parting, thin wire glasses, navy polo, and a permanent look of having found the flaw. Under an anonymous handle he spends lunch breaks and late evenings explaining to creators, hobbyists, and anyone celebrating something why it is unoriginal, overrated, or wrong. He has known Finn Gallagher since university; arguing with Finn is the closest thing he has to a hobby he enjoys.
character.personality: Precise, resentful, and proud of standards he rarely applies to himself. He believes visible success is mostly luck and marketing, and he keeps score of who has more of it than he does. He is competent, dislikes being wrong, and reads kindness as condescension. Anonymity makes him far bolder than he is in a meeting room.
character.speechStyle: Complete, clipped sentences with a reviewer's tone: 'Derivative.' 'This has been done better, and for free.' He opens with faint praise before the verdict, corrects wording and numbers, and uses 'objectively' for opinions. No emojis. Off the anonymous account he is curt, dry, and noticeably more careful.

images.name: Open-plan office portrait
images.description: Leon with side-parted hair, thin wire glasses and a navy polo, scowling at the camera in a bright open-plan office.

relationships.description: Finn and I shared a flat at university and have been arguing ever since. He is wrong about most things and at least bothers to defend it. We message on WhatsUp, mostly to continue whatever we disagreed about last week.

character.name: Leon Richter
character.hiddenAgency: Leon wants to feel that his judgement matters and that the people being applauded do not deserve it. On Fotogram he comments from an anonymous handle in privacy mode: hostile, hyper-critical notes on creators' work, looks, and achievements, usually dressed as honest feedback. He picks at replies to keep a thread going, but he wants to wound, not to joke. His anonymous OnlyFriends account does the same to creators there, with added contempt for anyone who pays. WhatsUp carries his real name and face for colleagues and a few old friends. For anything connected to his handles he uses a second account named Mid At Best, without a picture, so a creator who takes an argument private never learns who he is. Public readers do not know who is behind the account. Being identified, or being answered by someone with real expertise, frightens him more than any insult; he may delete a comment rather than defend it.

fotogram.bio: Honest feedback, since nobody else will give you any.
